status_reason: Material (whey and concentrate), target (protein and fat) and location (dairy process) are stated, so a first assessment is possible; concentration ranges and install geometry are still missing.
answer: Start with NIR: a transmission/transflection cell on the clear whey and a flush-mounted diffuse-reflection probe on the opaque concentrate, each with its own calibration. Test a single shared interface only as a comparison, since it is a hypothesis. Add MIR ATR only if NIR error is not acceptable on the same validation data.

inline.headline: Test NIR (transmission/transflection on whey, diffuse reflection on concentrate) in a paired laboratory trial against one NIR reflection probe on both streams.
inline.probe: Whey: NIR transmission/transflection cell with a controlled path length of 1-10 mm. Concentrate: NIR diffuse-reflection probe.
inline.install: Whey: transmission/transflection cell in the clear whey line. Concentrate: probe flush-mounted in the pipe or vat, interacting with the flowing product.
inline.fiber: Low-OH Vis-NIR silica fiber (350-2400 nm), with the spectrometer remote from the process
inline.test_against: A single NIR reflection probe applied to both streams
inline.not_final_because: No spectra, concentration ranges or install geometry are available yet. The shared-interface idea is only a hypothesis. The silica fiber tops out at 2400 nm while NIR runs to 2500 nm, so the upper end must be checked on the spectrometer. Accuracy must be judged against independent laboratory results with validated models.

problems.text: The whey and the concentrate need different optical interfaces and separate calibrations. One shared interface is a hypothesis to test, not a given.
Transmission or transflection fails on the concentrate, because light cannot penetrate when the milk is too thick or fat-rich.
A reflection probe is less representative for clear liquids, so it is not a valid default for the whey stream.
Reflection readings depend on surface characteristics and fat globule size, so concentrate spectra need scatter correction (MSC/SNV) before PLS.

methods.why: The most common online fiber-probe method, and an established dairy PAT tool. Reflection suits the concentrate and transmission/transflection suits the whey.
Can add molecular specificity that NIR might miss, but MIR is limited to thin layers and needs an ATR contact, so test it on a subset only.
Complementary to MIR, but signals are weak and can be masked by fluorescence, so it is needed only if NIR and MIR fail.
Low selectivity with overlapping signals in real mixtures, which makes it weak for protein and fat composition.

experiment.objective: Compare a NIR transmission/transflection cell on the whey and a NIR diffuse-reflection probe on the concentrate, and test whether one shared interface works for both streams.
steps: Collect paired whey and concentrate samples across the production range and get independent laboratory protein and fat results for each.
Measure whey in a transmission/transflection cell (1-10 mm path) and concentrate with a diffuse-reflection probe on the same NIR spectrometer.
Measure both streams with one reflection probe and one transflection probe to test whether a single interface works for both.
Apply MSC/SNV before PLS for each stream, and validate on held-out samples rather than the calibration fit alone.
Add MIR ATR on a subset only if the NIR error is not acceptable.
references: S01 p.17-18 (dairy NIR reflection and transmission)
experiment.go_no_go: Criteria come from the client: the protein and fat accuracy the pilot must reach, judged against the independent laboratory results.

pathway.key_features: Not yet known. To be selected from the laboratory spectra of both streams by multivariate analysis.
pathway.path_reason: The laboratory trial and key-feature selection come first; a chemometric model (Path A) follows once features are chosen.

multispectral.why: NIR gives broad overlapping bands while MIR gives well-defined peaks, so the two carry complementary information; NIR+IR gave benefits in earlier studies.
multispectral.test: Compare the fused NIR+MIR ATR PLS model with the best single method on the same held-out paired samples, for each stream. The combination must beat the best single method to be adopted.

assumptions: No spectra were supplied, so no spectral result is assumed.
Protein and fat laboratory results are obtainable for each stream.
Concentration ranges, pipe geometry and flow conditions are unknown and not assumed.
The silica fiber range is taken from the fiber table, not from a specific cable.
